tickets.title: parallax-background needs a 2.2.0 that a browser can compile — three changes, all proven by the r20 spike
tickets.detail:
The r20 spike compiled this game to JavaScript and ran it in Chrome (commit 8eee3f1, docs/browser-target.md section 10). To do it, tools/browser-spike/build.sh patches a COPY of parallax-background 2.1.0's published sources, because the artifact cannot be translated by GWT as it stands. Those patches are the change the library needs, and the library is Simon's own — published from the Parallax board, which this session cannot reach ('atelier --project parallax list' returns nothing here). So this ticket is the message in a bottle: someone with that board should carry it over.

WHAT 2.2.0 NEEDS, all of it proven by the spike:

1. ParallaxLayer must not use Cloneable. It declares 'implements Cloneable' and its clone() calls super.clone(); GWT emulates neither, and this is NOT dead code — ParallaxPageReader:55 calls layer.clone() on the real drawing path. The fix is a field-by-field copy; build.sh writes the whole replacement out, copying texRegion into a new ArrayList and then the fourteen scalar fields.

2. The Kryo and Jackson annotations have to come off the model classes the game touches: WholePage_Model, Parallax_Model, Page_Model, ParallaxLayer (@DefaultSerializer, @JsonIgnore, @JsonIgnoreType, @JsonIgnoreProperties and their imports). Kryo is reflection and Unsafe; it has no browser story at all. The game's own vendored copy already ran without them before ad38949 deleted it.

3. The serializers should be out of the translatable path: GVars_Serialization, Color_Serialize

tickets.title: Phase 2.1 — the lobby service: hold lobbies, mirror endpoints, gate on version
tickets.detail:
Online plan phase 2 (docs/online-multiplayer.md sections 2, 5 and 7). The small always-on process
WE host — no game logic, sees only endpoints.

WHAT IT HOLDS. {join code, host endpoint candidates, player count, game version}: list, join,
mirror each peer's public endpoint to the other for the punch, gate on protocol version, reap
dead lobbies. Under ~500 lines and a $5 VPS. Netty is a reasonable choice here (it is overkill for
the game socket); plain Java is fine.

THE TRAP THAT WASTES A WEEK, and it is decided: the client talks to the lobby service over the
SAME UDP socket the game will use. The public ip:port the service sees is then free STUN and is
exactly the mapping game traffic will arrive on. A second socket for lobby chatter advertises an
endpoint that does not work — and it fails only for other people, never on your own machine.

KEEPALIVES: a NAT mapping expires in about 30 s, so an idle lobby connection needs a packet every
5-15 s or a lobby that sat two minutes cannot be joined.

This service is ALSO the WebRTC signalling server for browser players (d7, see 2.6) — that is
decided, so do not design it as UDP-only inside.
Note (fedora1-lachassegalerie-22): Started: reading plan doc sections 2, 5, 7 and jks.net / jks.online before designing the service.

tickets.title: Phase 0.2 — give the world a fixed size and make the window a viewport onto it
tickets.detail:
Online plan phase 0.2 (docs/online-multiplayer.md section 6; the constraint is section 1.5).

WHY IT BLOCKS ONLINE. Nine places multiply Gdx.graphics.getWidth()/getHeight() by
GVars_Camera.worldMutiplier to get a world position: the camera ortho, hero spawn
(PhysicSpriteHeroes:77), the canoe (PhysicSpriteCanoe:34-35), the three spawners
(GVars_Game:93-115), the parallax, the star. A 1920x1080 host and a 1280x720 client therefore do
not share a world: the host spawns monsters off the client's map and the canoe is somewhere else.
The host sends world coordinates and the client must be able to draw them.

WHAT TO DO. Pick one world size in world units (the current 1280x720 * worldMutiplier is the
obvious one, so nothing moves at the default window) and give the camera a libGDX Viewport, so
the window only decides how much black or how much crop there is, never where anything is. Then
fix the nine sites to read the world, not the window.

WATCH OUT. The parallax world is sized from the window once at init (#background), and the game
is deliberately not resizable because of exactly this. Changing it is the point, but a Viewport
means resize() now has to mean something.

replays deaths=21 monstersKilled=81 — if this refactor is meant to change nothing, those counts
are the proof. Then play it at 1280x720 AND --fullscreen on a big monitor and compare where the
canoe, the spawns and the HUD land

tickets.title: Phase 1.4 — HostSession and ClientSession over loopback
tickets.detail:
Online plan phase 1 (docs/online-multiplayer.md section 6). The piece that makes two processes
play the same game, with NO lobby, NO NAT and NO internet.

WHAT TO DO. HostSession owns the sim, applies remote inputs at the tick they claim, broadcasts
snapshots at 20 Hz, and treats join and leave as network events — the game already lets people
join and rejoin mid-run, which maps straight onto it, ONE HERO PER CONNECTION (d5 -> A).
ClientSession sends inputs at 60 Hz, interpolates between the last two snapshots (~100 ms buffer)
and owns no physics.

KEEP IT FREE OF 'THE HOST IS ALSO A PLAYER' (the #network pack is explicit): a headless host with
zero local heroes must be a legal configuration, or the dedicated-server option becomes a rewrite.
Everything goes through the Transport interface from 1.1 — no DatagramChannel call anywhere in
session code, or browser players (d7) cost a phase to add back.

GATE. Two JVMs on one machine over loopback, plus the in-process host + 2 clients test that
asserts the clients' entity positions track the host's within tolerance. Both belong in the
nettest gate.
Note (fedora1-lachassegalerie-9): BLOCKED BY d10 -> A (r51): phase 0 finishes before any more netcode. Simon settled the order and it is binding — r32 (a world that is not the window), r33 (PlayerId instead of Controller), r34 (session teardown), r35 (one seeded RNG) and r36 (the headless runner) land first, and this ticket is p5 until they do. The count grows by about 11 a minute (115 after 10 minutes), with no upper limit. Heroes already die at y<0 (PhysicSpriteHeroes.act); potions need the same rule. It also matters online: r37's snapshot is capped at 1200 B, so the snapshot view must not send them.

tickets.title: Phase 1.2 — the wire protocol: input frames up, snapshots down
tickets.detail:
Online plan phase 1 (docs/online-multiplayer.md sections 4 and 6). Builds on 1.1's Transport,
which moves opaque bytes and knows nothing about the game.

WHAT TO DO. Define and implement the packet layout, as a pure codec with no sockets in it:
  - INPUT (client -> host, 60 Hz): a tick number and an input bitmask, plus THE LAST THREE INPUT
    FRAMES in every packet. That is what removes the need for any reliability layer on input.
  - SNAPSHOT (host -> clients, 20 Hz): tick, then the entities. Budget from section 4, at 8
    connections: hero ~13 B (pos, vel, hp, flags, anim, score), axe ~6 B, monster ~7 B, potion
    ~6 B, plus canoe, story clock, parallax offset and header ~20 B — about 430 B total.
  - JOIN / LEAVE / HELLO / keepalive, and a protocol version byte that the lobby can gate on.
Positions as 16-bit fixed point, ids 16-bit. Keep a packet under ~1200 B or IP fragments it, and
have the codec say so out loud rather than silently emitting 1400 B.

MEASURE BEFORE SIZING (risk 4 in the plan): monster spawns scale with heroes.size(), so 8 players
means far more bodies than the 430 B estimate assumes. Run the headless loop with 8 players and
count the entities before fixing the layout.

GATE. Round-trip tests in the nettest gate added by 1.1: encode -> decode -> equal, every field;
a truncated and a corrupted packet must be rejected, not misread; and the real entity counts from
a headless 8-player run must fit the budget.

There are four static Randoms: GVars_Story, GVars_Game, Index_Sprite, PhysicSpriteCanoe. They are
